h: Fill Your Durham Day Before the Lanes
p: Durham might be small, but it punches well above its weight. The cathedral and castle stand together on a rocky peninsula wrapped by a loop of the River Wear, and together they form a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The cathedral is a masterpiece of Norman architecture and the resting place of St Cuthbert, and the views from the river paths below are some of the finest in the North East.

The riverbanks are lovely for a walk any time of year, and in warmer months you can hire rowing boats on the Wear for a bit of fun on the water. Durham Market Place is the heart of town, and the cobbled streets winding up towards the cathedral are full of cafés and independent shops.

If you've got a car or a little more time, Beamish, the open-air museum recreating life in the North East over the past couple of centuries, is a short drive away and makes for a fantastic family day out.

At Lane7, the usual tips apply. Bowl with a ball you can comfortably control rather than the heaviest one going, look at the arrows on the lane rather than the pins, and keep your swing straight. Mix beginners in with stronger players to keep teams fair. And with students making up a big chunk of the city, term-time evenings can be lively, so getting a lane booked in advance saves a wasted trip. Then enjoy the rematch.
